issues.quote: **Step 0, this week, no build:** STL on for after-hours inquiries, appointment and credit-app types off; dated plan to the CSM.
issues.concern: Step 0 only works if forwarded leads reach resolveStlGate with a per-type external_type. The doc's own Evidence line says SPEED_TO_LEAD website leads can skip per-type config (isAlwaysAllowStlLead :406, Q19), and nobody has found any code that writes external_type from parseAdf (Q18, search_columns 0 hits). If either holds, 'credit-app types off' is a no-op: every forwarded lead, credit apps included, lands on DEFAULT or the bypass and gets the standard sales opener. That is exactly the credit and PII exposure the dealer ruled out (E5), shipped 'this week'.
issues.because: `conversational-ai-backend:src/speed-to-lead/services/speed-to-lead-console-call.service.ts:406` (isAlwaysAllowStlLead, confirmed via find_symbol), `:422` resolveStlGate; solution-context.md 'What a change would touch' (no writer of external_type); Q18, Q19; E5
issues.ask: Gate Step 0 on two checks before STL goes on: (a) the prod values of STL_ALWAYS_ALLOW_SOURCE / STL_ALWAYS_ALLOW_LEAD_TYPES and the source/external_type of a test forwarded lead on this team, (b) one sample forwarded email per type through POST /email-parsing/test-parse. Until both pass, make the control deterministic on the dealer side: the dealer forwards inquiries only (they already choose what to forward, E9), and say so in Step 0.

issues.quote: **Step 2:** opener template per lead-type entry; no template keeps today's opener. No-PII on credit-app is platform logic.
issues.concern: 'Template' has no data contract. The opener today is LLM output from one global prompt (generate :159, renderPrompt :441), so a 'template' could mean literal text sent verbatim or an instruction fed into the prompt. Those are very different builds and very different compliance postures. For credit-app the acknowledgment should be fixed text that bypasses the LLM, not a prompt hint the model may paraphrase. Also unstated: field name and type on speedToLeadByLeadType, which merge variables are allowed (appointment date, time, store), and what happens when a variable is missing (an appointment lead with no parsed time must not send 'see you at undefined'). The field must also survive both config writers and the DTO whitelist (Q20).
issues.ask: One line in Step 2 fixing the contract: literal vs LLM-guided per type (credit-app literal, no LLM), allowed variables, fallback to today's opener (or no send) when a required variable is missing, and that the field is optional and round-trips both upsertSpeedToLeadSettings and upsertStlFollowUpConfig.

issues.quote: Reply and follow-up share the generic prompt; without the type they confirm, then push a new appointment (Q12).
issues.concern: This is listed as a risk, but it is a scope item. STL_FOLLOW_UP goes through the same generate and decideTopic (:389), and the SMS reply path calls resolveStlGate from sms-v2 (:1955) with no evidence it carries lead type into the agent context. If Step 2 ships only the opener, the appointment lead gets 'confirming your 3pm' then a generic follow-up asking them to book. Step 2 as written would visibly fail the dealer's core ask (E5, E6).
issues.ask: Move it into Step 2 scope: lead type and appointment context are passed to follow-up generation and the reply agent, or the appointment and credit-app types keep follow-up off until they are. State which one.

issues.quote: **Step 3, full value:** CRM-first read, plus write-back of conversation and confirmed appointment through a channel agreed with the dealer.
issues.concern: Not challenging the full-value intent, only its design. Two problems. First, 'CRM-first read' has no meaning for this dealer: they have no API (E12), so the read source is the forwarded ADF, and the doc should say so rather than imply a CRM integration. Second, write-back into a dealer system with no failure design: no idempotency key (a conversation updated three times must not create three records), no retry or dead letter, no alert when a write fails at 11pm, no rule for a partial write (conversation sent, appointment not). The graph shows no existing outbound ADF-email or generic-webhook writer, so this is a new integration we would own and get paged for.

issues.ask: Reword Step 3 to name the read source per dealer type (CRM API where certified, forwarded ADF otherwise) and add one line that the PRD must specify idempotency key, retry and dead-letter, failure alert, and partial-write handling for the write-back channel before it is sized.
